primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic Nephropathy – End‑Stage Chronic Kidney Disease (Stage 5)
nice_guideline_used: NG203 – Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management

medications.duration: Lifelong — review renal function & potassium in 2 weeks, then every 4 weeks
medications.purpose: Renal protection and blood pressure control (already prescribed)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension; monitor creatinine & K⁺ after 1‑2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid panel review in 3 months
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a risk‑equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 5 mg once daily (titrate to 10 mg after 2 weeks if needed)
medications.duration: Lifelong — BP review in 2 weeks, then every 4 weeks
medications.purpose: Achieve BP target <130/80 mmHg in proteinuric CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 BP target <130/80 mmHg when ACR ≥70 mg/mmol; CCB appropriate when eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.dose: 20 mg once daily (adjust up to 80 mg BID based on volume status)
medications.duration: Lifelong — electrolytes & renal function review in 1 week, then monthly
medications.purpose: Control volume overload/edema in stage 5 CKD
medications.nice_justification: Standard CKD management; safe in eGFR < 30 and recommended for fluid control

medications.dose: Continue current regimen as titrated to glucose targets
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control for type 2 diabetes with advanced CKD
medications.nice_justification: Essential diabetes management; insulin is safe in eGFR < 30 (NICE NG28)

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood‑pressure lowering effect; risk of symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Start amlodipine at low dose, monitor BP and symptoms after 2 weeks

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential for intravascular volume depletion and rise in creatinine
interactions_checked.action: Check serum creatinine, eGFR and electrolytes within 1 week of initiation; adjust dose if needed

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined antihypertensive effect may increase risk of orthostatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Monitor standing BP after dose changes

interactions_checked.interaction: Loop diuretics may cause hypokalaemia, which can potentiate insulin‑induced hypoglycaemia
interactions_checked.action: Monitor serum potassium and glucose; supplement potassium if low

contraindications.reason: Thiazide diuretics are ineffective and may cause hyponatraemia at eGFR 9 mL/min/1.73 m²
eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of lactic acidosis
Accelerate CKD progression and increase fluid retention in stage 5 CKD
Not indicated when eGFR < 20 mL/min/1.73 m² (patient eGFR 9)
contraindications.alternative: None; insulin remains primary glucose‑lowering therapy

assumptions_warnings: Serum potassium not provided – assume ≤5.0 mmol/L; will check after any ACE‑I dose change.
Baseline liver function tests not available – required before starting atorvastatin.
QRISK score not available – CKD stage 5 qualifies patient for statin regardless of QRISK.
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I, statin or CCB allergies before prescribing.
Volume status not quantified – loop diuretic dose to be titrated based on clinical assessment.
treatment_summary: Continue ACE‑I (lisinopril) for renal protection, add atorvastatin for CV risk, introduce amlodipine to reach BP target, replace ineffective hydrochlorothiazide with furosemide for volume control, and maintain insulin for diabetes. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, BP, lipids and glucose as per NICE NG203 recommendations, and avoid contraindicated agents such as NSAIDs, metformin and SGLT2 inhibitors in this eGFR 9 patient.
